gallery.title: File:Congress Hotel CMHD.JPG
gallery.description:
Congress Hall Hotel, Beach Drive between Congress and Perry Streets, in Cape May, New Jersey. Built in 1879 after a fire destroyed the previous hotel on the site. Located in the Cape May Historic District, a National Historic Landmark since 1976. This may be the most important building in the district, as it and its predecessors have been the big tourist draw to the town, or at least one of the first and largest hotels.

gallery.filename: Alfred Jacob Miller - Beach at Cape May - Walters 372675.jpg
gallery.title: File:Alfred Jacob Miller - Beach at Cape May - Walters 372675.jpg
gallery.credit: Walters Art Museum:  Home page  Info about artwork
gallery.description:
Cape May, New Jersey, is among the oldest American seaside resorts, hosting vacationers from the mid-Atlantic region from the 18th century forward. In this drawing, Miller pokes gentle fun at leisure travelers. Two men seated on folding stools sit on the sand despite clouds of annoying insects. The caption reads:
Consolation for the afflicted!-who cannot go to Cape May,-viz-
"Can't get away Club", -"when there is a land breeze,-two gangs of 

mosquitoes are laid on!!-the wide-awake squad, reserved for the night!!!"
